transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Rao (Redwood); Dr. Rahul Patel, Sofia Gomez, Ethan Park, Nina Alvarez (HelioMed)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style health check: review of uptime incidents, token burn and cost drivers, and product roadmap alignment for next-quarter rollouts. Plan: agree on pilot sizing for dedicated pool, identify quick wins to reduce per-token spend, and confirm security/compliance artifacts for procurement.

Topics:
- Recent availability blips (week of 2/9)
- Token burn spike during A/B rollout
- Dedicated vs Hosted for regulated workloads
- SOC2/KMS/data-retention questions for procurement
- Roadmap: model rollouts, canary strategy, cost optimization (quantize + caching)

Transcript body:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes, quick check-in from HelioMed on usage and any problems. Rahul, do you want to kick off with what you saw last week?
00:14 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): Yeah, thanks Maya. We had a couple of small outages, like a 4-5 minute window where chat endpoints returned 503s. It coincided with our A/B rollout of the new triage model, spike in traffic, and then some retries. We logged higher 99th pct latency too.
00:31 Speaker 3 (Liam): Can you share the traces? was that routed to hosted, or did it hit your Dedicated pool?
00:37 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): Hosted. We didn't move to Dedicated yet. It's on our roadmap but finance wants the burn number.
00:45 Speaker 4 (Ethan): From infra, the spike looked like a behavioral change in sequence length—some prompts hit 2.5x token length unexpectedly. KV cache hit rate dropped because of new conversation prefixes.
01:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): Okay that tracks. On the Redwood side we have automatic fallback policies but if noise shifts sequence length distribution, batching and kernel selection can miss the target. We'll ask Liam to sketch how Dedicated pools with static exec paths would behave.
01:18 Speaker 5 (Liam): Right, Dedicated gives more predictable latency SLOs because you pin model variants and avoid noisy multi-tenant scheduling. But the trade is commit and cost. We can reduce per-token cost a lot with quantization plus prefix/KV cache tuning.
01:37 Speaker 6 (Nina): Finance here—our main ask is a clear three-scenario cost model: baseline (current hosted), optimized (quantize + batching), and peak (sales events). We need to show ROI to legal and procurement.
01:51 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll do that, Priya will help map the usage signals into cost buckets. We'll also surface burst capacity options so you can keep a hosted fallback for spikes.
02:03 Speaker 3 (Liam): Quick note on cache misreads—sometimes transcribers show K-V cash instead of KV cache, so you'll see weird wording in logs, but the metric is simple: cache hit % directly affects tokens served. If hit drops from 85% to 50% you can multiply token spend by nearly 1.6x.
02:23 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): Ugh, that explains the burn spike. We rolled out a small feature that added user context to prompts, which increased average length. We should have flagged that.
02:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): No worries, that's common. Actionable: Ethan send those traces and a sample of changed prompts. We can run them through a quick traffic profile to show impact.
02:45 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Yep I'll drop a packet to Maya and Liam after the call.
02:50 Speaker 5 (Liam): On the reliability side, two options: 1) move high-sensitivity endpoints to Redwood Dedicated with SLA and reserved capacity, and keep the rest in Hosted with autoscaling; 2) keep Hosted but add circuit breaker + canary size control and a guaranteed burst budget. Option 1 better for deterministic latency.
03:10 Speaker 6 (Nina): Price delta on Option 1? We need monthly committed spend numbers.
03:17 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll model that in the 3-scenario doc. We'll include a sample Dedicated sketch: GPU pool size, expected qps, and fallback policy for overflow to Hosted.
03:28 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): On compliance—our procurement wants to see SOC2 and KMS integration. Are those straightforward?
03:34 Speaker 3 (Liam): Yes, Redwood Private has KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments, and Hosted supports customer-managed keys in some regions. We can share our SOC2 report and our whitepaper on data flow and audit logs. Priya will push the artifacts.
03:49 Speaker 5 (Priya): I'll drop the SOC2 export and the KMS notes, but note we redact customer-specific material; still, it satisfies procurement checklist usually. Also we'll include retention settings and log export patterns.
04:05 Speaker 6 (Nina): Legal will ask about egress and data residency—HelioMed needs EU-only storage for certain PHI-derived models. Can Redwood do EU-only?
04:14 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we have region pins and Private deployment options. For strict residency we usually propose Private (VPC or on-prem). It is slower to stand up, but it's an option. We'll add timeline/examples to the artifacts.
04:26 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): Timeline wise we want a pilot in Q2 and full roll by Q3 if numbers work. Success criteria: 99.9% uptime, 99th pct latency below 600ms for triage endpoint, and a 30% reduction in per-token cost vs current baseline after optimizations.
04:47 Speaker 5 (Liam): 600ms 99th is achievable on Dedicated for those model sizes; on Hosted it depends on concurrency and routing. We'll show numbers.
05:01 Speaker 6 (Nina): Also call out retention and audit log retention for regulatory.
05:07 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. Now let's step through the cost levers quickly: batching, quantization, KV prefix caching, and routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical calls.
05:19 Speaker 3 (Liam): On quantization—moving to 4-bit or mixed precision can cut runtime by 30-50% but watch hallucination risk. We'll suggest a small eval set to measure quality delta.
05:34 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): For triage it's okay if there's slight variance, but we need to monitor false negative rates. We'll want a roll-forward/roll-back plan tied to eval metrics.
05:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): That's our Optimize playbook—continuous evals with threshold alerts. We'll link a template.
06:00 Speaker 4 (Ethan): A couple practical questions: how do you handle canary traffic split? We saw our traffic tool couldn't split by user cohort easily.
06:09 Speaker 3 (Liam): Redwood Console supports per-route rollout, canary percentages, and automatic fallback if error rates or latency cross thresholds. It also tags tokens per-route for cost analytics. You can join rollout control with your feature flag system.
06:26 Speaker 6 (Nina): Show me cost tagging—finance needs to know which feature drove the spike.
06:31 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll surface token-level breakdowns in the cost model. Priya, can you add a sample CSV with per-route token burn?
06:39 Speaker 5 (Priya): Yep, I'll include a sample.
06:44 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): Any concerns about vendor lock with Dedicated? We don't want to be stuck if model requirements change.
06:52 Speaker 3 (Liam): Good question. We recommend an abstraction: pin at model-version level but keep a fallback variant compatible with runtime. Also we keep the same API semantics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so switching is lower friction.
07:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Let's outline the pilot scope: 6-week pilot, Dedicated for triage endpoint (reserve enough capacity for 2x normal peak), run quantization experiment on canary traffic, and measure cost/latency/qa. If results meet criteria, plan Q3 rollout.
07:21 Speaker 4 (Ethan): 2x peak reserved is a lot; any suggestions to reduce commitment?
07:26 Speaker 3 (Liam): We can do committed baseline with a burst pool you pay for when used—keeps commitment lower but increases unit price for burst. We'll show both in the cost doc.
07:37 Speaker 6 (Nina): What's the expected monthly burn reduction if cache hit improves from 60% to 85% and we add quantization?
07:45 Speaker 5 (Priya): Rough ballpark: 25-40% reduction depending on model mix. We'll put exact numbers in the cost scenarios.
07:54 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): For our team, next steps: we'll share traces and a sample of the changed prompts. Finance will want the cost model and procurement the SOC2 docs.
08:04 Speaker 1 (Maya): Confirming action items: Ethan share traces, Maya + Priya produce cost model, Liam prepare Dedicated sizing, Priya share SOC2/KMS notes. We'll also schedule the dedicated sizing call with your infra folks.
08:18 Speaker 4 (Ethan): I'll get the traces in the next 24 hours.
08:22 Speaker 6 (Nina): We'll review the cost model with legal and revert.
08:27 Speaker 3 (Liam): One more operational note: we suggest adding a token cap per-user to protect against prompt injection or runaway prompts driving cost. It's a small config flag in the Console.
08:40 Speaker 2 (Dr. Rahul): Good point—I'll loop in product on enforcing per-user caps.
08:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Anything else?
08:48 Speaker 5 (Priya): I'll include a link to the sample rollout checklist and a short runbook for autoscale events.
08:55 Speaker 6 (Nina): No further items. Thanks.
09:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks everyone. We'll circulate the documents and lock the next call for Dedicated sizing next week.

Closing notes (auto-generated style, may be imperfect):
